HTEAM-CTX-G1.title: Juniper weekly sync notes, 8 September
HTEAM-CTX-G1.text:
Juniper weekly sync - notes
Date: Tuesday 8 September 2026, 10:00-10:45
Chair: Marcus Oyelaran (engineering manager)
Attendees: Hana Kobayashi (backend), Tomas Reyes (data engineering), Leila Farrokh (QA), Dev Anand (product), Siobhan Walsh (Finance Ops)
Notes taken by: Leila Farrokh

1. Shadow run results
The shadow run has been comparing new-pipeline invoices against Ledgerd output since 7 Sept. Reconciliation diff rate is 0.4 percent against the 0.1 percent target agreed with Finance Ops. Hana traced most of the diff to currency rounding in the proration path (mid-cycle plan changes on non-USD accounts). The remaining diffs look like timezone boundary issues on usage events stamped near midnight UTC.
Decision: extend the shadow run by one week. The shadow run now ends Friday 25 September instead of 18 September.

2. Cutover approach
Discussed big-bang versus staged. Siobhan and Leila both preferred staged, because Finance Ops cannot manually review more than about 300 invoices per day if something goes wrong.
Decision: cutover will be done by customer cohort, not all at once. Cohort A is internal accounts plus 40 friendly customers, then Cohort B (roughly 2,000 accounts on monthly plans), then everyone else. Dates per the plan, adjusted for the shadow-run extension - Marcus to update the plan.

3. Scope
Dev raised that Design has been mocking up a new invoice PDF layout.
Decision: the invoice PDF redesign is out of scope for Juniper and moves to the Q1 backlog. Dev to tell Design.

4. Rollback
Decision: keep Ledgerd running in read-only mode for 30 days after the final cohort is cut over, so any invoice can be regenerated from the old system if needed.

5. Pricing-table freeze
Siobhan asked whether pricing-table changes should be frozen during cutover. Not decided. Siobhan to check with Revenue and bring an answer to the next sync (15 Sept).

6. Go/no-go sign-off
Open question: who signs off on the Cohort A go/no-go. Marcus suggested Dev; Dev suggested Finance Ops should, since they own the reconciliation tolerance. Left open.

Risks raised
- Stream bus consumer lag spikes at month end. Tomas saw 11 minutes of lag on 31 August with the current 12 partitions.
- The tax provider API is rate limited to 50 requests per second; the historical backfill may get throttled if it runs alongside live traffic.
- Leila is on PTO 28 Sept - 2 Oct, which overlaps the planned Cohort A window. No QA backup named yet.

Action items
- Hana: fix currency rounding in the proration path. Due Thursday 17 Sept.
- Tomas: backfill script for March-August usage events; dry run on staging by 22 Sept.
- Leila: reconciliation dashboard showing diff rate by cohort. Due 21 Sept.
- Dev: tell Design the PDF redesign moved to Q1; update the roadmap page.
- Siobhan: ask Revenue about a pricing-table freeze; answer at the 15 Sept sync.
- Marcus: confirm on-call coverage for cutover weekend with the SRE lead (Ines Duarte); update plan dates.

Next sync: Tuesday 15 September.

HTEAM-CTX-G2.title: Project Juniper plan v3
HTEAM-CTX-G2.text:
Project Juniper - plan v3
Owner: Marcus Oyelaran. Last updated: 1 September 2026.

Goal
Replace the nightly Ledgerd batch invoicing job with an event-driven pipeline on the Stream bus, so usage shows up on a customer's draft invoice within 5 minutes instead of the next morning, with zero double-billing.

In scope
- Usage event consumers for metered products (API calls, seats, storage).
- Proration and plan-change handling for monthly and annual plans.
- Historical backfill of March-August usage events into the new store.
- Reconciliation tooling against Ledgerd during shadow mode.
- Cutover runbook and rollback procedure.

Out of scope
- Invoice PDF template redesign.
- Multi-currency discount rules (tracked separately by Revenue Engineering).
- Changes to the customer-facing billing page.
- Tax calculation logic (we call the existing tax provider as-is).

Milestones
M1 Event schema frozen - 21 Aug (done)
M2 Shadow run - 7 Sept to 18 Sept
M3 Cohort A cutover - 29 Sept
M4 Cohort B cutover - 13 Oct
M5 General cutover - 27 Oct
M6 Ledgerd decommission - 30 days after M5

Dependencies
- SRE (Ines Duarte): increase Stream bus partitions for the billing topic from 12 to 24 before M3. Requested 25 Aug, not yet scheduled.
- Tax team (Rafael Lindqvist): refresh tax provider sandbox credentials before the backfill dry run. Current credentials expire 20 Sept.
- Finance Ops (Siobhan Walsh): sign-off that the reconciliation diff is within the 0.1 percent tolerance before each cohort.
- Data Platform: no schema migrations on the usage warehouse during the week of each cutover.

RACI
Accountable: Marcus Oyelaran
Responsible: Hana Kobayashi (pipeline and proration), Tomas Reyes (backfill), Leila Farrokh (QA and reconciliation)
Consulted: Siobhan Walsh (Finance Ops), Rafael Lindqvist (Tax)
Informed: Grace Mbeki (Support lead), Dev Anand (Product)

Risks
R1 Month-end traffic spike overwhelms consumers. Likelihood medium, impact high. Mitigation: partition increase (SRE dependency); avoid any cutover in the last 3 days of a month.
R2 Backfill throttled by the tax provider rate limit. Likelihood medium, impact medium. Mitigation: run the backfill overnight, capped at 40 requests per second.
R3 Reconciliation diff does not reach tolerance. Likelihood low, impact high. Mitigation: extend the shadow run; do not cut over any cohort while the diff is above tolerance.
R4 Support unprepared for invoice questions. Likelihood medium, impact low. Mitigation: support briefing one week before each cohort.

Success measures
- Usage event to draft invoice line in under 5 minutes (p95).
- Reconciliation diff at or below 0.1 percent for two consecutive weeks before general cutover.
- Zero double-billed invoices.

Not covered in this plan
Budget, vendor costs and headcount are tracked by Marcus separately and are not part of this document.

HTEAM-CTX-C1.title: Juniper leadership status snapshot (draft)
HTEAM-CTX-C1.text:
Juniper - status snapshot for leadership (DRAFT, forwarded by Dev Anand, 14 Sept)

Summary: GREEN. The shadow run is going well and the diff rate is now 0.1 percent, within target. Cohort A cutover is locked for 22 September.

Detail

Shadow run: started 7 Sept. The latest daily reconciliation shows a diff of 0.3 percent, mostly rounding on non-USD accounts; a fix is in progress with Hana.

Cutover sequence: Cohort A (internal plus friendly customers), then Cohort B, then general availability for everyone else. Cohort A target: 29 Sept. Cohort B and general dates to be confirmed once Cohort A has run for a full billing cycle.

Scope: the invoice PDF redesign ships with Cohort B, so customers see the new layout on their first event-driven invoice. Design has final mocks.

Owners: Hana - pipeline. Tomas owns the reconciliation dashboard. Leila - QA.

Owner table
Workstream | Owner
Pipeline and proration | Hana Kobayashi
Backfill | Tomas Reyes
Reconciliation dashboard | Leila Farrokh
QA | Leila Farrokh

Rollback: Ledgerd stays available for two weeks after the final cutover, then it is switched off.

Infrastructure: the SRE partition change for the billing topic is done.

Asks for leadership: none at this time.

Risks: none blocking. Month-end volume is being watched, and Support has been told to expect a few questions from Cohort A customers about the new invoice timing.

Next milestone: Cohort A go/no-go, sign-off by Marcus.

items.answer: Fix forward works when the blast radius is small and we can watch it in production. Here the retry change touches too much of the pipeline, so a bad deploy could take down more than the retry path itself. I'd rather ship the smallest safe slice now and fix forward on that, or hold the rest for next sprint. Which do you want to commit to?
